a defect called over the bar whose open item says worth: no gets a new worth: later item that names the old one, the old one unchanged, listed under Filed in the backlog, with no second review and no new run of the checks

a defect seen again gets the item that holds it named by Jev before anything is filed: alike names it for a builder, file stops and writes no file of that run, --same files nothing for it and files the other, Jev is asked nothing twice, and with no key every item is listed to read

a defect that two rounds saw word for word is one item, also under the suffix of its place, and two defects of one place and title with two runs are two; file refuses a worktree with a change nobody committed

a line the session wrote by hand under Seen, not filed with no bar call stops propose, which names the line and says to give it a bar call and a reason or to file it; with under and its reason it goes on
a new item in the backlog folder after a review keeps the review, and an edit of an item that was on the base asks for another

a repository whose team settings say findings = false under [jev] sends no finding to Jev, with a key on the machine, and each line of a finding under the bar says Jev was not asked, off in the settings

a review judges each defect outside the change by the bar: one over it is an item with worth: later, one under it an item with worth: no that ends with the review's reason and is listed under Filed as not worth it, each other one is a line under Seen, not filed, a cheap one that a fix line names by its number left out, and no new run of the checks; with no JEV_API_KEY each line of a finding under the bar ends with Jev: not asked (no key)
a task started from a backlog item stops at propose while its branch holds the item, and after a builder's git rm and a new run of the checks the review still covers it and the pull request opens
an item that was on the branch before the review proves nothing; an item that was filed and then removed stops propose with its path and the two ways on, and file --again puts it back
an item the owner set to worth: no, with his reason in it, is still the item of the same defect when the next round sees it again: nothing is filed over his no

file refuses a defect named by both --same and --new, and a number of no waiting defect, before Jev is asked or a file is written; --new files the defect as its own item and leaves the item Jev named as it is

Jev reads each finding called under the bar once, an under item and a notes line, with the bar from rule 6 and none of the agent's reasons; a read over the line stops propose one time and names both, the second propose goes on and asks nothing again, each line ends with Jev's score, and a landing that starts over keeps the read
the items land.py file commits after the gate ask for no gate again: the request is proposed and lands with them on the gate's one run; an item written by hand after the gate asks for the gate

the merge agent's brief lists each item the branch adds to the backlog, the builder's and the review's, by its path and title, and names the file of the bar the project's builders read: Lem's in the plugin, or the project's own lem-builder.md
the review is told of the branch's items, and a defect it lists at the place of an item the builder filed gets an item of its own, as a defect of another place does

two rounds that saw defects outside the change give their items in the backlog's format, each round's committed alone by land.py file; a second run files nothing; propose waits for each, and the pull request names each item

a branch changed after its push, whose pushed head the forge merged, keeps its local copy and loses the forge's, and clean names the commit that changed, also for one space that git's patch id does not see, and the commands that show and remove it, not a commit made on the forge

a branch the landing rebased after its push, whose pushed head the forge merged, goes with the forge's copy, also when the base moved next to a line it changes, and clean says it was a rebase after the push of the same commits
a branch the landing rebased after its push, whose pushed head the forge merged with a merge commit, goes with the forge's copy, and clean says it was a rebase after the push of the same commits

a careful change after a conflict: the read of the resolution finds nothing and nothing carries; propose says that a fresh merge agent reads it because the request is careful, and the owner's merge given before the conflict ends with that reason
a careful change keeps its review through a rebase with no conflict, onto a base that left its files alone and onto one that changed one of them in other lines

a conflict after a merge: base stops on the files of the pull request the forge calls conflicting, and after a builder's resolution base keeps the polish pass by its new names; the resolution gets one read that is no round, which finds nothing in the change and files what it saw outside it, so the merge review from before the conflict carries to the resolution's tip and the owner's merge stands; propose keeps the pull request, and its text and the proposed event say what carried

a first push onto a branch a teammate pushed meanwhile is refused with his commit named, and an open pull request on the task's branch name whose head Lem did not push is not taken: its number and author are named, and its title, text and branch stay his

a new task's worktree starts from origin's base branch after a fetch, with no upstream, while the local base branch is older; a second call finds it; with no remote, or an origin that does not answer, it starts from the local base branch, and the second says so on stderr
a proposal that the forge's step refused writes no proposed event and keeps the task in landing, with no gh on PATH named as such and a forge's error said; the next proposal is the one event
a pull request a commit on the base made conflicting: start --conflicting brings it onto the base, and its text says why
a pull request closed on the forge with no merge ends its task: merged writes it dropped with the line that says so, and clean removes the worktree and keeps the branch with its commits
a pull request is merged through the forge, only at the commit that was proposed and that the caller saw, and the main checkout follows
a pull request is not merged over a base that moved; one the owner merged on the forge as one commit is finished by its own step, also while the task has the landing line again
a pull request whose base was changed on GitHub is not merged, with the branch it has named and the command that puts the base back, and a merge into that branch is not written down as landed
a task is not opened under a slug whose branch origin has already, by its semantic type or by the name --branch gives, and one whose branch is free opens

a task whose landing starts over starts its reviews over and keeps its pull request; a second proposal changes the one that is there, also when the record of it was lost: the forge is asked, and no second one is opened; a merge with no pull request on record is refused, and nothing reaches the base past the forge

a teammate's commit on the task's branch stops base before its rebase, also after a plain fetch, naming its commit, author and subject and the pull that takes it in; then it is part of the change: the checks and a read come again, and the push keeps it

after a merge an open task with no conflict waits as it is; the owner's word to land it is refused on the moved base with the steps, and they bring it onto the new base: the polish pass and the review it had stand through a rebase with no conflict, the checks run again, and propose pushes it and keeps its pull request, whose text and state say what happened in one line

after a merge the forge made as one commit, the branch goes only when it holds nothing that was not merged; a deletion the forge refuses is an error that keeps the local branch; the forge's copy stays when it holds a later commit, whatever another branch with the same last words holds; and a run with nothing in the way removes both

after an Update branch on the forge and a merge as one commit, clean says that the forge merged a commit made on the forge after the branch's tip, not that the branch has commits after it, keeps the branch, and names the one command that removes it
after the merge the worktree and the branch go, the forge's copy of the branch too

an open task whose last review left a must-fix that no review read after its fix: the rebase onto the moved base keeps why no review covers the change, and propose ends the owner's merge with that reason
an origin that is not on GitHub: init refuses it with the line that points it there, and propose refuses before it writes or pushes anything
merge merges no pull request whose head on the forge is not the proposed tip, nor a closed one, and names the step for a closed one

merged on a pull request that is still open keeps what the forge says of a conflict on the pushed head, and waiting gives conflict beside green: null before any look and when the head moved, false, then true
with a GitHub remote the branch is pushed and a pull request is opened with the title and the text, and the task is open with its address

a branch with no commit of its own is refused by base with the step that ends the task; clean deletes a dropped task's branch the base holds, and keeps one with commits of its own, with how to delete it
a file that was untracked before the gate is not removed: the gate refuses the worktree, and start refuses it as before
a file with no suffix is read with the marks of the language its first line names, a Python script and a shell script each with its own, and a file with no such line with none
a gate command's process group ends with it, so a process it left behind is ended; a gate that is stopped ends the command that runs and what it started, says so, and keeps no result

a gate command that writes a cache folder and a file git does not know passes: the gate removes them and the folders they emptied, keeps the tracked folder, names them in its output and in one line of its log, and records the tip
a gate with no command to run refuses, and records no green tip
a green result is for the commands that ran: with none left, or one more, in the main checkout's settings, propose asks for the checks again; with the same, it proposes
a landing lock that cannot be opened, read-only or a folder, stops start with its path and says to remove it, with no traceback
a landing record that is not JSON stops a step with its path and no traceback, and moving it aside, the state ready and start begin the landing again

a landing task whose worktree is gone holds no other task back: another task starts its landing beside it, and the task's own step names the git commands that put the worktree back, and each works as named

a rebase of base that git refuses with no file in conflict, by a hook of the repository, is refused with git's words and leaves the worktree and the record as they were; once the hook is gone, the same step rebases
a rebase of base whose abort leaves HEAD detached is refused with what is not as it was and the command that puts it back, never with words that the worktree is as it was
a task branch the owner protected after its worktree was made gets no push from propose, and clean removes neither it nor the worktree until the name leaves branch.protected

a test file moved out of the tests lowers the bar as a deleted one does, and so does a mark that runs one test or group alone, named without the call's parenthesis; a word that only ends the same way is none
an ignored __pycache__ that was there before the checks goes before their first command and is named in the result only; .env, a cache inside an ignored folder and one a command writes stay
base refuses a worktree where a builder's own rebase is in progress, names how to finish it or end it, and aborts nothing

propose refuses notes that are no file and a title of two lines before it writes anything; merge refuses a gated commit and a tip other than the ones on record, and no record of a gate; after a commit past the proposal the steps the refusal names land the new tip
start refuses a worktree on no branch and names the switch that puts it back on the task's branch; after it, start takes the task

--stop ends the checks during a command, during a serial command that takes its wrapper's cleanup to end, and during the criteria's tests, with no process left, no file the command left untracked, no worktree of the criteria's check, no result kept, the lock free and a gate.end of stopped; with no run it stops nothing

the bar sees a deselect, a -k not, a rerun and an ignore pattern in a runner's settings, a coverage threshold that went down and a flaky decorator; the checks name each existing test, snapshot and test configuration the change edits
the check of the criteria refuses a branch with no commit beyond the base

the gate refuses a command that edits a tracked file, one that makes a commit, and a criterion's test that passes on the base commit, and records no green tip for any; a green gate records the tip and that tip's tree
three starts at one moment take turns under a lock, and each of the three tasks starts its landing: no task waits for another's
two writers of one file at one moment each write a new file of their own: neither fails, the file is one text whole, and no new file is left

while the checks run, a second run is refused because they already run, base, read and propose wait for their end on a tip that passed before, and --status says they run; while another step holds the lock the checks are refused with its name; each run ends with one gate.end and its line
with no command in its checks start blocks the task and says to add the commands and run start again, which then takes the task it blocked

a complete request that someone else wrote, by its brief or a state line, is not proposed with only the lead's freeze of a read in which nobody was confused; the owner's approval after the read lets it through, and the checks say that the criteria waited for his yes and when he gave it

a criterion a pick of the dialectic removed and one the lead added are not green, each with its line first, what it was or is, its reason and the decision that led to it, which is on record; the gate refuses the plan until both are recorded; and the checks say that two model families read the criteria, when he approved them, and that a change of the build came after the read

a full change whose criteria name only the developer lands with no read on his recorded word and his approval after it: green, with the line that the personas did not read them on his word and that he approved them; his word with no approval after it is refused
a full change with his approval and no read is refused when no word of his to skip the read is on record, and a word of Lem's in the same form is no such word

a full change with no read of its criteria is not proposed, nor one whose newest read flagged a criterion or split the families with no approval of his after it; a partial read counts and says who did not answer and why; and criteria he changed after the read are one line that is no cause of not green

a plan that says Size: small is refused by the criteria, the polish pass and the gate, also with Lem's approval of a small change in the owner's name; the refusal names the small change, which has no plan, and the full change's Size line

a read by the lead with one model family in which nobody was confused is one line of the checks, which says the build did not wait for him, and the scout's facts are named with no path of this machine; a read's event without its form, with fewer than two personas asked, with nobody or more than were asked answering, or with a missing source unnamed is refused, and nothing is written for it; the lead freezes the plan's criteria the read named, with no file of other criteria, and from then on a change of them has its record, while the line still says the build did not wait for him
a read freezes only the first contract of a task: a second clean read of other criteria freezes nothing over a read's contract, and a read never replaces his approval or its size

a read in which nobody answered is written down with no family and each source named, and started once more: after one the request is not proposed and the criteria are not frozen; after the second the build goes on, the criteria are frozen as read, and the request is not green with that reason first

a read of the criteria as a recorded change made them is the read of the criteria now, and no line says otherwise; a change he approved afterwards stays in the pull request with its reason and the personas' answer, marked as approved by him, and is no cause of not green

a request is never proposed over a breaker that waits, also under a ready written over it; the owner's help settles it and is no cause; a pick of the dialectic and a decision of one expert alone are each a line of the text that is not green, the text lists the breaker and each decision of the record and names the one expert, and the merge agent does not merge it
a request that had an interview is not proposed without the owner's approval of its criteria, also after a read that found nobody confused and the lead's freeze of it; his approval lets it go, green

a request with a changed criterion is not green: its text says so first and shows the change, with what the criterion was and is, and the owner merges it whatever the settings say, through its pull request, and the main checkout follows
for a full change from a complete request his word to skip the read is refused: a lead that started before his word, or before his approval after it, wrote the criteria, and the personas read them
without the owner a flagged criterion the dialectic rewrote is approved by:alone as the ladder left it, and the request is proposed not green, with the decision and the change after the read

without the owner the criteria are approved by:alone, never while the task runs with him, for the small change of his own request or over his approval; a flagged read of someone else's request with such an approval after it is proposed
a branch that commits the machine's own settings file is careful by the script: the full set, a line of the pull request that says the file is one machine's own, and a person's merge

a branch that edits the flow table of its own settings is careful by the script, which says why, gets the full set and a person's merge, and the landing reads the main checkout's topics, also when it runs from the task's worktree
a branch that removes Lem's own settings is careful by the script, and the reason says that it removes the file

a change of documentation only is not proposed without a review; a review that nobody answered is started once more, and after the second the request is proposed as not reviewed, which the merge agent does not merge; the record of a review agent that ended with no files is the session's, with no careful call
a change of one space, or the same edit in another place of the file, is another change by its id, and a change that came back to what was reviewed is the same change
a change that adds a suppression is refused at the checks, which name the file, its mark and the plan's section for the reason, and no review starts

a full change's checks waits for the polish pass; polish prints the range of the task's own commits from the base, the plan, the report, the interview's outside.md, the backlog folder and the files the pass may not change, and keeps the tip it starts at, also when it is started again after the builder's first commit

a plan of more than three tasks gets a round at the least; the plan's careful call is read under its title only, never from a line its plan talk quotes, a yes gets the full set, and a later commit that takes the yes back leaves it; a plan with no task list is refused, not taken for a small one
a polish pass that was done stays done when a red base held the task and it starts again on a base that moved: polish says done, the checks find the pass by its new name, and no second pass starts

a request the review calls careful and its plan did not gets the full set, its text says first that a person merges it and why, says in its checks that it had no plan talk and why, the plan's miss is one event with the review's reason, and no agent merges it; a record with no careful call is refused

a task that ran without the owner is not green for each thing of his decided without him, one line each: criteria approved without him, a decision of the experts or of the dialectic, and one no level settled

a task that ran without the owner with nothing of his decided without him is green, and says when it ran so and on whose words; the gate's and the personas' decisions stay green, with the cite and the count of votes and families; the merge agent reads it and merges it while he is away, as any other

every edit of Lem's own settings is careful by the script: one of [branch] gets the full set, a line of the pull request with the table named and a person's merge, and one of the file's text alone is careful too

polish --done refuses a worktree with changes, a pass that changed a criterion's test file, and one after which the tests of the criteria no longer hold; otherwise it runs them, logs one polish event with the tips, the commits and the items filed, and a pass is done once
polish logs polish.start once, with the tip the pass starts at, and not again when it is started a second time before --done

the checks on the tip the polish pass ended on run no test of the criteria, keep the pass's result with the pass and its commit, and their gate.end names that commit; after a fix on top, and after a rebase by base, they run the tests themselves once, on the new tip
the gate finds the polish pass on its tip with a fix on top of it, refuses a branch rewritten under the pass, and after a rebase by base knows the pass's last commit by its new name
the merge agent merges a green request whose newest review says not careful, and its text says the review's call with its reason; a newest review with no call leaves the merge to the owner

the owner's careful on a task whose pull request is open: start takes it into the landing again, the review is due again with the full set, and propose writes the text again, careful, so the owner merges it
the pull request's checks say how many commits the polish pass made and how many items it filed, and that the tests of the criteria were taken from the pass at its commit and not run again

with a reason for each file in the plan the gate passes, and the request is still not green: the review says what it thinks of each reason, the text opens with each lowered bar, its reason and the review's word, the event log counts it, and no agent merges it

a base run again after a propose cut off after its push moves nothing and keeps the notes of the rebase that made the tip: the merge review carries, the owner's merge stands, and the pull request says rebased on main

a base that moved after the checks is read by a fresh merge agent with the commits and the files that moved beside the change; its read covers the base its brief named, so an answer recorded after main moved again covers no later base and the merge waits for a new read; a safe read merges with no new run of the checks and keeps what moved, and the merge commit, the pull request's text, pr.md and the task's state name the base the checks ran on, the base it merged on and the read's why, also when the edit of the text failed once; the squash commit's body names the fix on the way before that line and ends with the task; a merge GitHub refuses writes no line

a base that moved back under a tip a rebase made keeps no note of that rebase: the review is read again, the merge review does not carry, the owner's merge ends, and the pull request does not say the review carried

a base that moved by a document is refused too; landed again, the merge review carries onto the new tip and the owner's merge that the base refused stands, so it merges through GitHub after the re-check: the main checkout fast-forwarded, the state landed; the task began on the release before this one, as its mark says, and Lem stopped none of its steps

a builder's rebase that stops on a later commit too: the resolution names the files of each stop by their own names, café.txt too, every file whose patch the rebase changed, a binary file whose content the resolution changed too, for the read of the resolution, and not a binary file the base left alone
a builder who resolves the conflict with the rebase base named keeps the commit the base took out again, and the next base takes his resolution
a commit added after the proposal stays on the branch through the two rebases of a red base, and propose ends the owner's merge with the reason one rebase with no wait gives
a commit after the rebase that follows a red base ends the owner's standing merge: propose prints ended with that reason, never null, and logs merge.ended once
a commit subject is refused when the branch's own commits land

a conflict on the rebase after a red base is met from the tip proposed before, and its resolution with a read that found nothing carries the merge review and the owner's merge on a request that is not careful; on a careful one his merge ends with the careful reason
a conflict with the base names its files and leaves the worktree as it was
a file moved on the base counts as a change of the path it left, and the merge is refused

a first task that brings the gate on its own branch, while the main checkout's settings have none, is gated by it and is not green for it; a branch that changes a gate the main checkout has is gated by the main checkout's; either is careful by the script, which says why, so it gets the full set and the owner merges it
a fix is reviewed only after the machine checks ran on it, and the second round knows the first
a landed task does not land again
a merge agent that ends twice with no answer on the checks' own base, after a revert, answers no refusal: it calls the owner, the refusal of his merge stays, and his merge does not stand

a merge agent whose seat fails after the pull request is open: the fallback stands in on the same brief, the record names the seat kept with it whatever the settings say by then, the pull request's text and pr.md get its line once; a stand-in that fails too blocks the task, and a merge on GitHub while it waits lands it, its line replaced by the one that says it failed too

a merge GitHub refuses says GitHub's line, keeps it for the list of what waits for the owner, and lands nothing; on his word, with history = squash, the branch then lands as one commit, and its tree is the tree the gate passed on

a merge whose real parent on GitHub is not the base the read covered names the base it merged on and says that no read covered it, in the pull request's text, the task's state and a line for the owner

a move of the base that a revert undid after Lem refused the owner's merge: the read's brief names the checks' own base, its read answers the refusal, and his merge stands and goes through with no new run of the checks

a plan of four tasks with no plan talk is not proposed, though another task's talk is in the log; a talk's event without its form is refused, the bound among its fields too, which the log adds itself, and nothing is written for it
a project with no gate command lands nothing, and the task is blocked instead of holding the landing line

a read that says another round merges nothing and keeps a base refusal that no later read answers, also when the move touched a file the change edits; a second answer with no base call on a moved base is recorded as another round, and the step's next line, the kept refusal, the brief's and the merge's refusal say that its answer could not be recorded, never that it said so; the new landing carries the merge review with no call on the old base and merges with no line
a rebase that changes nothing of the change does not undo its review
a red gate exits 1 with each command's result, the later checks do not run, and nothing is read or proposed on it
a request that came from a bug names in its checks the cause its investigation found, with its place and no path of this machine

a request that is not careful with a must-fix gets a round after its fix, with each profile it ran or left out and why; after two rounds no third is taken, the request is proposed as not green, which its first lines say with the reason, and the merge agent does not merge it
a request the owner called careful after its plan is proposed with no plan talk, its checks say in words that it had none and why, and that is no cause of not green

a request the owner called careful gets the project's full set: a record of less is refused, one that leaves a profile out too; a round in which one source did not answer counts, and a must-fix is followed by another round

a request whose plan says careful is not proposed while its event log has no plan talk, and the refusal names the plan stage's step, the talk the task's lead opens, and the event its defender writes in the form project.py takes
a resolution whose changed line and whose commit's subject hold a byte that is not UTF-8 is read like any other: base takes it, with no traceback

a review is written down from a file, with its round, its kind, who answered and its counts; a record that does not have the form, the number of this review or the tip it is of is refused, and a change that was reviewed clean is not reviewed again
a review whose record is sent again, after a cut-off run or by mistake, is written down once and takes one round
a safe read of a moved base still calls the owner for a careful request, and the merge agent merges nothing

a second rebase after a red base starts again from the tip proposed before: the commit git left out of the first rebase, onto a base that repeated its edit, is on the branch again once the base reverted it, and the owner's merge stands for the whole change

a start over moves the review files of the landing before into reviews/landing-N/, N one more than the folders there, so the new review writes over none of them and the record of the old review, of the same attempt and tip, is no record of the new landing, at its old place or in its landing's folder

a talk's counts agree: each question of the list ends settled or open, a design choice is an open one, and a question gets one repair at most; a talk over its bound of 4 × questions + 2 turns, or with more decisions two questions named than design choices, is written as it ran, with the bound the log adds; a talk of no question and two turns has nothing raised after its list; the start of a talk names its reviewer and nothing else, and a refused record writes nothing

a task started from a reviewer's item of the state folder removes the item's file when it lands, by Lem's merge and by merged; a removal that fails leaves the task open and merged removes it; a pull request closed on GitHub drops the task and leaves the file
a tip proposed on a base that then went back carries no merge review to that base: the proposal keeps the base it was made on, the reason names both, and the merge review of that tip no longer counts

after its plan talk a plan of four tasks is proposed, and its text holds one line of the talk, from the newest event, with its turns over the bound when they are, each of its counts in words, and a count Lem has no words for by its name

after its plan talk a request whose plan says careful is proposed, and the checks of its text say who argued the plan with its defender, the turns, the positions settled and left open, and the other counts of the talk
after the commands the gate proves each criterion's test on the branch and on the base commit, looks for a lowered bar and counts the size
after the merge on GitHub the state is landed, and a main checkout that cannot follow is reported with git's own reason
an open task takes the landing line again, and a new base forgets the gate's result, so nothing is proposed or landed before a new one
base on a git whose range-diff takes no path refuses with what failed and the fix, and keeps nothing, the polish pass's names among them
base rebases onto the remote's base branch and says how many commits the branch adds
base run twice with no move of the base in one landing keeps one rebase from the tip proposed before, and the owner's merge still stands

base runs the plain rebase and carries the review only where git's merge of the base and the tip before is clean and is the rebased tip's tree; otherwise a read is due with the paths and each commit the rebase left out; a stop goes to a builder with the rebase that applies every commit, a change lost inside a merge commit is refused with the tip that puts it back, and an ignored file keeps its bytes
clean refuses a task that has not landed
clean removes a landed task's worktree and its branch in one run
clean removes an answered task's worktree and leaves its branch, which may hold the test that reproduced the bug, with how to delete it; the report stays
clean removes the landed task's branch when its worktree is already gone, keeps the task's state, and a third run finds nothing left
gate runs every command with its output in a file, keeps the last line, logs each result and records the green tip
merge refuses when the base moved by a file, and names the merge agent's read of what moved as the next step
no step runs on a task that did not take the landing line, and the owner's word lands nothing that was not proposed
no step runs toward a branch the settings refuse

nothing is proposed before its review; for a request that is not careful the floor is one read, and a reviewer gets the owner's words, the plan, the range, the rule files of the changed files, the project's topics, the items of the backlog and the folder of the review tool

Jev key (optional) — Check for JEV_API_KEY. The key is required if correction collection is on.
agdoc skill (recommended) — a page about an issue, a plan or a change that the owner asks for himself, to read in agterm
agterm (required) — Find agtermctl, read its version and report whether this is an agterm session.
agterm skill (required) — Find the installed agterm instructions.
backlog skill (required) — the owner's own view of the backlog items in docs/backlog/, and the picker that adds and opens them
board notifications (optional) — Read the device subscriptions and the last push result.
board server (optional) — Read the server's addresses, process, log and code version. Report when the installed code replaces it.
claude (required) — Find Claude Code and read its version.
codex (recommended) — Find Codex and read its version.
codex persona agent (optional) — Find the Codex persona definition in the user configuration.
correction hook (project) — Look for an older correction hook alongside the plugin hook, and give the applicable removal step.
cronn (required) — Find cronn, read its configured port and report whether its status API answers.
gh (optional) — Find the GitHub CLI and report whether it is signed in.
git (required) — worktrees, branches and the task state directory
handoff tokens (optional) — Read the token threshold that compacts the task's session.
hook modules (required) — Check the plugin hook launchers and the app modules and imports they need.
installed Lem (optional) — Compare each workspace's installed plugin code with the board server code.
lem plugin scope (project) — Report a user-scope Lem install that loads in every repository.
lem-builder agent (required) — Find the Lem builder definition Claude Code can use.
load gate (optional) — Read the machine's load gate settings and show the configured and current load.

mailbox-chat (required) — the wake-up of a task's idle session by the board's server (a merge, a conflict, its turn in the queue) rests on its waiter, the owner's hook; and the messages between the defender and the reviewer of a plan talk
mailbox-chat skill (required) — how an agent sends to the other pane and reads what comes back
permission mode (project) — Read the effective permission modes of a new session and a background builder.
plannotator (recommended) — the Inbox carries what waits for the owner while he is away, to his phone too, and brings his answer back into the task's session
plannotator-tui (recommended) — the owner marks up what a pane printed, or an agent's newest reply, from two agterm chords
project personas (project) — Read the effective project cast. If there is one persona, say that a panel needs a second.
python3 (required) — Check that the Python interpreter meets Lem's minimum version.
revmux (required) — the review rounds before the pull request, with the project's profiles and lenses
revmux skill (required) — how an agent runs a review round: it writes the round's context and reads the findings back
task picker (optional) — Find the agterm keymap chord that runs Lem's task picker.
webrev skill (required) — the owner marks up a plan, a draft or any document as a rendered page, and the notes come back to the agent
At startup with the door enabled, check the local Tailscale state and bind a separate loopback listener. Publish the matching HTTPS entry or keep it if already set.
For each tailnet request, check the board host and the owner's Tailscale login. Refuse Funnel requests and cross-origin actions.
During a relayed peer stream, check every 0.5 seconds for client disconnect or local shutdown. Close the peer socket when either occurs.
Before the board command opens a workspace or task page, run ensure and use the server address it reports.
When a Claude Code startup or resume hook finds a repository with Lem team settings, start a detached ensure without holding up the session.
After a push service reports 404 or 410, remove that subscription. Keep the last push results for the server status.
When a sent note no longer matches or an unsent item no longer qualifies, remove it from the local record.
When an eligible blocked task needs the owner's direction, send its state and ask what to do or whether to drop it.
For an eligible breaker, send its document or summary with Help, Park and Drop.
For an eligible merge wait, send the pull request, the full proposed commit and why the merge agent calls the owner. Offer Merge or Not now.
When a task waits for the owner to resolve its order, send a text question that asks which task it follows.
For other eligible waits, send the task's state and the board's instructions for the owner as a text question.
For an eligible wait for plan approval, ask Build or Drop and attach the plan when it is available.

Start a separate merge job when the review of the proposed tip says merge, calls nobody and needs no new checks for a moved base. Skip a current refusal, a forge conflict or a merge already in progress.
Start the owner's standing merge when a safe read or a new landing preserves the owner's word for the present tip. A new refusal, a conflict, a required new round or a merge in progress holds it.
At startup, use the local Tailscale name when available. Keep the short host name as an alias if it differs. Otherwise use the short name.
Open a session for a queued task when its predecessor ends, the board knows no session lives, and none opened during this wait.

At a forge tick, ask GitHub about relevant open pull requests in a real workspace with a GitHub remote. Look the first time and after at least 180 seconds. Save mergeability and the head for the board and conflict wake.
Every 10 seconds, check each real workspace with known session status. Read the Inbox status while the owner is away or a sent item remains on record.
When the board requests peer lists and a peer's last look is at least 5 seconds old, fetch its workspaces in parallel with other due peers. Keep the last answer and record if the peer is unreachable.
At a forge tick, read the live task sessions and find the worktrees of ended tasks in each real workspace with settings. Refresh the board when a session need or a held task's work changes.
At the first forge tick and every 3600 seconds after the last run, prune a real workspace whose settings read. Apply state.keep_days to old files and summarize eligible ended tasks.
When a server merge ends, record its outcome for the board. The note can report a merge that stands after a base change. Clear the active merge and refresh the workspace.

Every 5 seconds, detect newly waiting rows in real workspaces. Use the first row's action and task link, with a count of further rows, in one push per device whose workspace filter matches. A first look sets the baseline. A row that returns within 300 seconds sends no second push.
When the owner runs lem serve --push-test, send a test push to every subscribed device.
When a subscribed device asks for a test from the board, send that device a test push.
On a requested main-port change, stop the old server for this home before the new configuration takes effect.
When the forge reports a closed pull request and this server does not hold its merge, record the task as dropped and keep the branch. Retry a failed bookkeeping call after 300 seconds.
When the forge reports a merged pull request, run the landing bookkeeping if this server does not hold its merge. Retry a failed bookkeeping call after 300 seconds.

After the status wake and 10 more minutes without work, log the stop when Lem cannot read the session's signs or the restart is already spent or blocked by a stop. The board then shows the stop if it still stands.
When the door sees a login that differs from the remembered owner, reread the current login at most once per 30 seconds. Recheck the request if the login changed.

Every 0.5 seconds per open workspace stream, check the event log, owner mark, settings, backlog, Inbox and selected task files. Send a refresh on a change or when a board act, session look or forge look changes the workspace.
When a stream opens with an old rendered version, a since query or Last-Event-ID, send a refresh at once.
When a board listing needs workspace counts, recompute them if the cached counts are at least 5 seconds old. Recompute the active workspace's counts for its page.
When a request reads a joined machine's page, file or stream, pass the read to that peer and relay its answer. Record a failed connection as unreachable.
When a request needs peer state or a named peer, reread the machine's peers table. Refresh the local peer objects when a name or port changes.
When a watcher or board listing asks for workspaces, reread the registry. Reuse a workspace when its name and path match. Include only workspaces with a state directory.
When the owner turns the door off or moves it to a different port, remove Lem's old Tailscale entry if it still points at its loopback door.

When ensure finds a server for this home with a different door setting or install identity, stop it and start the caller's install. The identity uses the version, build commit and real package path. With no build commit, it also uses the newest module change time.
On an eligible Lem command, run a detached ensure if the board's PID file has no live process and LEM_SERVE is not off.
After a status wake and 10 more minutes without work, open a fresh session if the signs read, no stop stands and the restart for this stretch of work remains available.
After a duty command fails, retry when it is still due after 300 seconds. A merge retry belongs to the proposed tip and its review.
After a send gives no answer, retry on a later look with the same payload and key while the owner is away, the door is open and the wait still matches.
At each 20-second forge tick, run the forge, session and retention jobs for each registered workspace with a state directory.

While away with an Inbox tailnet address, send a board link and the cause when a new wait has no session that can answer or is ineligible for a question. Cases include a missing, deaf or stopped session, a dropped predecessor, a refused or unreviewed merge and a release stop.

While the owner is away and the Inbox has a tailnet address, send a new wait with a live session that can answer. Use that Claude Code session and the task's own thread. The merge wait includes its review. Cards have their own board page.
When ensure finds the configured port free and LEM_SERVE is not off, start the detached server and wait for its answer.
On a local stop request, SIGTERM or Ctrl-C, end the background jobs and streams, close the listeners and remove the PID file.
On an open stream with no refresh for 10 seconds, send a ping with the log version.
Before a detached start, empty the server log if it is larger than 1000000 bytes. Append the startup identity and the child's output.
After an owner board act that needs to tell the task, send the live session a wake. The session command can open a session when the task needs one.
Wake an open task when GitHub reports a conflict on the head it proposed and that proposal has had no conflict wake or open.
Wake a task after its pull request merges or closes on GitHub, if its worktree remains and the end has had no wake or open.
After the Inbox accepts a new or retried question, wake the live session so it can show its card.
When a sent question names a session that no longer runs the task, read its thread. Wake the live replacement for a new owner reply and remember which replies it heard about.
Wake the live session of a queued task when its predecessor ends and no session opened or woke during this wait.
Wake an open task after a merge-agent refusal or after Lem refuses the owner's merge because the base moved. The refusal has had no later wake or open.

Ask a live task session for status after 45 minutes without work. If Lem cannot read its signs, use the task's events. The guard covers building, ready and landing tasks with a live agent and no shell command.

what: | `[seats]` | a seat or `fallback` for this computer, in the same form. It replaces the line of the team. `/lem set local reviewer codex/gpt-6.2-sol:high` writes the reviewer, and `/lem set local reviewer default` removes it |
| `[state]` | only `keep_days`: the days for the old files of this computer. Lem uses this number on this computer, also when it is lower or higher than the number of the project |
| `branch.base` | `/lem init` writes the default branch | the branch that a task starts from and lands on |
| `branch.history` | `"squash"` | what lands. `"squash"`: one commit. `"keep"`: the commits of the branch |

| `branch.land` | `"agent"` | who merges. A merge agent reads each pull request first and writes its review. `"agent"`: the merge agent merges a green pull request that is not careful, and calls you for each other one. `"owner"`: you merge each pull request |
| `branch.protected` | `[]` | the branches where Lem lands nothing, pushes nothing and deletes nothing, also a task's own branch that you add here later |
| `checks.commands` | `[]` | your tests, the whole suite. Add a linter only when no git hook runs it. With no command, only the task that adds one can land |

| `checks.serial` | `[]` | the tests that two tasks cannot run at the same time, for example an end-to-end suite with fixed ports. They run after `checks.commands`, one at a time for all tasks. Keep them out of `checks.commands` |
| `checks.setup` | `[]` | what a new worktree needs before its tests can run, for example `"uv sync"` or `"npm ci"` |

| `flow.topics` | `[]` | the topics, one sentence each: `"a customer is charged the wrong amount"`. `/lem init` proposes them from your code, and you correct them. A change that can affect one is careful |
| `jev.findings` | `true` | `false` sends no defect and no item of this repository to the model. The line of the defect then says "Jev: not asked (off in the settings)" |
| `paths.plan_file` | `"YYYY-MM-DD-<slug>.md"` | the name of a plan file |
| `paths.rulings` | `"docs/rulings.md"` | the file of your rulings, one bullet for each: `- **The rule in one sentence.** (YYYY-MM-DD)` under the `##` heading of its group |
| `seats.experts` | the list in `~/.config/lem/settings.toml`, else `["claude/fable:high", "codex/gpt-6.2-astra:high"]` | the experts of a decision in doubt. Without Codex, one answers alone |

| `seats.fallback` | the line in `~/.config/lem/settings.toml`, else `"claude/opus:high"` | the seat that Lem starts in place of the reviewer, the planner or the merge agent when its agent gives an error. Write all three parts. `false` turns the fallback off, and then the task waits for you |
| `seats.merger` | the seat in `~/.config/lem/settings.toml`, else `"claude/opus:high"` | the merge agent: `claude` or `codex` |
| `seats.planner` | the seat in `~/.config/lem/settings.toml`, else `"claude/opus:high"` | the defender of the plan in the plan talk: only `claude` |

| `seats.reviewer` | the seat in `~/.config/lem/settings.toml`, else `"claude/opus:high"`. `/lem init` writes `"codex/gpt-6.2-sol:high"`, or `"claude/opus:high"` without Codex | the reviewer of the plan talk |
| `seats.session` | the seat in `~/.config/lem/settings.toml`, else `"claude/opus:high"` | the agent of the session of each task: only `claude` |

| `state.keep_days` | `30` | the days after which an old file goes. When nothing of a task that ended happened for this number of days, the task keeps only its small record, and its events become one summary event. Lem counts from the last event of the task, and from the last write of a folder. A dropped task whose events became a summary cannot be resumed. A whole number, `1` or more. A computer can set its own number in `.lem/settings.local.toml` |
| `tracker.kind` | required | `"linear"` or `"github"`, the one key of the table. With `"github"`, Lem uses the issues of the repository that origin names |

| `corrections.collect` | `false` | `true` turns on [the correction queue](install.md#the-correction-queue) in every repository on this computer. `lem corrections collect yes` and `lem corrections collect no` set it |
| `handoff.tokens` | `600000` | the number of tokens where the session of a task compacts. `0` lets Claude Code compact at its own limit. `lem project handoff --tokens N` sets it |
| `load.start` | `40` | the load average under which the checks of a landing start. `lem project load --start N` sets it, and `lem project load --start none` writes `0`, which removes the limit |
| `peers.HOST` | none | the port of the door of another computer of the board, with its Tailscale name as `HOST`. `/lem serve join HOST` and `/lem serve leave HOST` write it |
| `serve.port` | `4536` | the port of the board server. `lem serve --port N` sets it |
| `serve.tailscale_port` | `4537` | the port of that door. `lem serve --tailscale-port N` sets it |
| `serve.tailscale` | `false` | `true` opens the door for your phone. `/lem serve tailscale` and `/lem serve tailscale off` set it |
| `ask.browser` | `false` | `true` opens the question page in your browser when you work outside agterm |
| `ask.review` | `"auto"` | the list of your answers before Lem gets them: `"auto"`, `"always"`, `"never"`, `true` or `false` |
| `ask.size` | `"auto"` | the size of the question page: a percent of the pane, `"auto"` or `"full"` |
| `ask.status` | `{asking = ["blocked"], answered = ["active"]}` | the status of the session while a question waits, and after you answer it |
| `ask.style` | `"refined"` | the look of the question page: `"refined"`, `"minimal"`, `"bold"` or `"terminal"` |
| `seats.reviewer`, `seats.planner`, `seats.merger`, `seats.session`, `seats.experts`, `seats.fallback` | as in [`[seats]`](#seats) | each seat and the fallback, in the form of [`[seats]`](#seats) |
